point: Inserted sentence: the next paragraph must follow from it.
插入句：下一段要能接著它說下去。
why: The blank ends paragraph 1. The first sentence of paragraph 2 says The elevator that remains in service will be busier than usual, so one of the two elevators keeps running during the work. The sentence that sets this up is Only one elevator will be shut down at a time, starting with the east one.

空格在第一段最後。第二段第一句說 The elevator that remains in service will be busier than usual，表示施工期間兩部電梯中有一部照常運轉。能先交代這件事的句子是 Only one elevator will be shut down at a time, starting with the east one（一次只停一部，先從東側那部開始）。

point: Find the noun the pronoun replaces.
找出代名詞代替的名詞。
why: Tenants on the lower floors are asked to leave … free for residents of the upper floors. What they leave free is the elevator in the sentence before: The elevator that remains in service. Paragraph 1 says only one elevator is shut down at a time, so just one is running. One elevator is singular: it.
低樓層住戶被要求 leave … free for residents of the upper floors。要留下來的，是前一句的 The elevator that remains in service。第一段說一次只停一部，所以施工期間只有一部在運轉。一部電梯是單數，用 it。

point: The clue for the linking word is in the next paragraph.
連接詞的線索在下一段。
why: The sentence itself does not decide; paragraph 3 does. It says the freight elevator is open to tenants for these deliveries from 6 to 8 a.m. each weekday. these deliveries are the furniture and large items in the blank's sentence, and 6 to 8 a.m. is its early in the morning. So large items may come in through the loading dock at that time; at any other time they are postponed: unless.

本句自己決定不了，要看第三段。第三段說貨梯 open to tenants for these deliveries from 6 to 8 a.m. each weekday。these deliveries 就是空格那句的家具和大型物品，6 點到 8 點就是那句的 early in the morning。所以大型物品在這個時段經卸貨區送進來是可以的，其他時間才要延後：用 unless（除非）。

point: Tense: compare the e-mail date with the start of the work.
時態：比較 e-mail 的日期和開工日期。
why: The e-mail is dated March 9, and paragraph 1 says the technicians will begin on Monday, March 16. The blank's own sentence says the freight elevator is normally used only by building staff. Opening it to tenants is a new arrangement for the work week, and it has not started yet: will be.
這封 e-mail 的日期是 March 9，第一段說技術人員 Monday, March 16 才 will begin。空格這一句也說貨梯 is normally used only by building staff。開放給住戶是配合施工的新安排，還沒開始：用 will be。

gloss.ex: The landlord sent a notice to every tenant.
Only two of the four buses are in service today.
We postponed the meeting until Friday.
The truck is waiting at the loading dock.
Use the freight elevator for large boxes.

point: A good result, then the step it leads to.
先是好結果，再是因此採取的行動。
why: The sentence before says the sales staff reported far fewer rejected claims than they had with the paper forms. rejected sounds negative, but far fewer rejected claims is good news: the trial worked. Because of this, Tallyway will replace the paper forms for everyone. The blank's sentence is the result of the one before: As a result.
前一句說業務部同仁 reported far fewer rejected claims than they had with the paper forms。rejected 雖然是負面字，但 far fewer rejected claims（被退回的申請少很多）是好消息：試用很成功。因為這樣，全公司都改用 Tallyway。這一句是前一句的結果：As a result。

point: The next sentence decides the adverb.
下一句決定副詞。
why: Receipts are now simply photographed with a phone, but the next sentence says Our auditors may ask to see the originals during the annual review. So the paper originals must be kept even after they are photographed: still.
收據現在 simply photographed with a phone 就好，但下一句說 Our auditors may ask to see the originals during the annual review。所以即使拍了照，正本仍然要保留：still。

point: Inserted sentence: link it to the sentences before and after.
插入句：前後兩句都要接得上。
why: The sentence before moves the deadline from the 15th of the following month to the 5th, an earlier date. The sentence after says claims that miss the deadline will be repaid the following month instead, and instead needs a usual case to contrast with. This earlier date lets us repay claims in the month they are submitted does both: it points back to the 5th and gives the usual case.

前一句把期限從 the 15th of the following month 提前到 the 5th，是比較早的日期。後一句說錯過期限的申請 will be repaid the following month instead；instead（改為）需要一個平常的情況來對照。This earlier date lets us repay claims in the month they are submitted（提前的期限讓我們在提交當月就撥款）兩邊都接上：指回 5 日，也交代了平常是當月撥款。

point: late is itself an adverb: submitted late.
late 本身就是副詞：submitted late。
why: The blank describes submitted, so it needs an adverb. The paragraph is about a deadline: claims must be submitted by the 5th, and these claims are repaid the following month instead. So they are claims sent in after the deadline, submitted late. late works as an adverb with no -ly.
空格修飾 submitted，要用副詞。這一段講的是期限：申請要 submitted by the 5th，而這些申請 the following month instead 才撥款，所以是過了期限才交的，也就是 submitted late（逾期提交）。late 不加 -ly 就能當副詞。

gloss.ex: We ran a two-week trial of the new software.
The bank rejected the loan application.
Submit your travel claim within thirty days.
The auditors checked every invoice from last year.
Travel costs will be repaid within two weeks.

point: Inserted sentence: the next sentence explains it.
插入句：下一句在解釋它。
why: The sentence before says orders have nearly doubled and the ovens now run around the clock, so Mill Road is working at its limit. The sentence after says The bakery sits on a narrow lot between a school and a row of houses: there is no room to build more there. The missing sentence is the point that this explains: Expanding the original bakery was never an option. That is why the company is opening a second site.

前一句說訂單 have nearly doubled，烤爐 now run around the clock，磨坊路的廠已經滿載。後一句說 The bakery sits on a narrow lot between a school and a row of houses：原址沒有空間再蓋。空格要放的，就是這句話在解釋的事：Expanding the original bakery was never an option（擴建原本的烘焙廠從來不是選項）。所以公司才要另開第二座生產基地。

point: Tense: the dateline shows March is past.
時態：報導日期顯示 3 月已經過去。
why: The sentence only says in March. The article opens with the date June 12, and the new bakery is due to open in October, which paragraph 1 calls this autumn. So this is March of this year, already past: began.
句子只說 in March。報導開頭的日期是 June 12，新廠 is due to open in October，也就是第一段說的 this autumn。所以這是今年的 3 月，已經過去了：began。

point: Time conjunction: the sentence before decides.
時間連接詞：由前一句決定。
why: The sentence before says The building has room for all of Corvell's pastry production, so Mill Road will eventually bake only bread. When the new site is fully running, it takes over all the pastries. So Mill Road can go on baking some pastries only in the period before that: Until the new site is running at full capacity.
前一句說 The building has room for all of Corvell's pastry production, so Mill Road will eventually bake only bread。新廠全面運轉後，糕點全部由新廠做。所以磨坊路繼續烤 some pastries，只會是在那之前的過渡期：Until（在……之前一直）。

point: given the opportunity to do something: a choice, not an order.
given the opportunity to + 動詞：是可以選擇，不是命令。
why: The sentence before says no current employee will be required to move. So moving to Southmere is a choice for Mill Road staff, not a duty. Those who want to move get the first chance, before the jobs are advertised: opportunity.
前一句說 no current employee will be required to move。所以調到 Southmere 對磨坊路員工來說是自己的選擇，不是義務。想調的人可以在 the jobs are advertised 之前優先申請：opportunity（機會）。

gloss.ex: The factory runs around the clock during the holidays.
The company bought an empty lot next to the station.
The conversion of the old mill into offices took a year.
The two offices will eventually move into one building.
The new plant will reach full capacity next spring.
She asked to transfer to the Boston office.

point: Same or different? Check the first paragraph.
相同還是不同？看第一段。
why: The first paragraph says the printed copy often arrives a week or more after the first of the month. The blank's sentence says the digital edition will reach you on the first of every month. The two editions differ, so the answer is Unlike.
第一段說紙本 often arrives a week or more after the first of the month。空格這一句說 the digital edition will reach you on the first of every month。兩種版本不同，所以用 Unlike（和……不同）。

point: Inserted sentence: join the price cut and the refund.
插入句：把降價和退款接起來。
why: The sentence before cuts the price from $96 to $72. The sentence after says some subscribers have already paid for next year and will receive a refund of the difference. They can get money back only if the lower price covers them too. The new rate will apply to all subscriptions, including renewals makes that link.

前一句說年費 from $96 to $72。後一句說有些訂戶 have already paid for next year，他們 will receive a refund of the difference。新價格也適用於他們，才會有差額可退。The new rate will apply to all subscriptions, including renewals（新費率適用於所有訂閱，包括續訂）正好把兩句接起來。

point: Take out our records show, then see what the blank does.
拿掉 our records show，再看空格的作用。
why: our records show is an extra phrase placed inside the clause. Without it, the sentence reads Subscribers … have already paid for next year. The blank comes right before the verb have already paid, so it is the subject of that verb. A subject that refers to people: who.
our records show 是插在關係子句中間的插入語。拿掉它，句子是 Subscribers … have already paid for next year。空格後面直接接動詞 have already paid，所以空格是這個動詞的主詞。指人的主詞用 who。

point: Should you + verb = If you + verb.
Should you + 原形動詞 = If you + 動詞。
why: After the comma comes an instruction: please check the box on the enclosed form. So the first half must be a condition. Should you prefer is a formal way to say If you prefer: if is left out and should comes before the subject.
逗號後面是指示：please check the box on the enclosed form。所以前半要是一個條件。Should you prefer 是 If you prefer 的正式說法：省略 if，把 should 放到主詞前面。

gloss.ex: Postage is included in the price of the catalog.
Fuel prices rose sharply last quarter.
The March issue includes a guide to local restaurants.
Customers can ask for a full refund within thirty days.
If the hotel costs more, the company pays the difference.
Please sign the enclosed contract and return it.
